small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_OC (e.g. 32/64) paired with BLOCK_N=64/128 and BLOCK_K=16/64 — current OC=16 only fills one BLOCK_OC tile, but increasing BLOCK_K to 64 (since K_TOTAL = 3*27 = 81) cuts the K-loop iterations in half and may improve `tl.dot` efficiency.
- Precompute `k_input_off` and `w_offs` once outside the K loop only if K_TOTAL fits in a single tile — with K_TOTAL=81, try BLOCK_K=128 (mask-out tail) to make the K-loop single-iteration and eliminate loop overhead.
- Swap grid axes so `pid_batch` is axis 0 (fastest-varying for L2 reuse of weights across batch); also try collapsing (batch, oc_block) into one grid dim to better balance 128*1=128 program count per spatial tile.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a channels-last (NDHWC) input/output layout so the IC*KD*KH*KW gather is contiguous along the K-dimension; this enables vectorized loads in the im2col gather and lets `tl.dot` consume packed K-tiles without strided gathers.
- Consider a persistent-kernel design with one program per (batch, oc_tile) that streams over the full ODHW spatial range internally, reusing the loaded weight tile (OC*K_TOTAL = 16*81 = 1296 floats — fits in registers/SRAM) across all output positions. This eliminates the redundant weight reloads currently done per spatial block.
- Alternatively, since K_TOTAL=81 is tiny, materialize an explicit unfold (im2col into a [N*ODHW, K_TOTAL] buffer) and call a tuned cuBLAS GEMM for the matmul, then run a small fused epilogue kernel — for small kernels with large spatial extent this often beats hand-rolled Triton GEMM.
